arxiv-2203-12264.title: ECO v1: Towards Event-Centric Opinion Mining
arxiv-2203-12264.creator: Ruoxi Xu, Hongyu Lin, Meng Liao, Xianpei Han, Jin Xu, Wei Tan, Yingfei Sun, Le Sun
arxiv-2203-12264.description: Abstract Events are considered as the fundamental building blocks of the world. Mining event-centric opinions can benefit decision making, people communication, and social good. Unfortunately, there is little literature addressing event-centric opinion mining, although which significantly diverges from the well-studied entity-centric opinion mining in connotation, structure, and expression.

arxiv-2206-03379.title: Semiconductor ring laser frequency combs with active directional couplers
arxiv-2206-03379.creator: Dmitry Kazakov, Theodore P. Letsou, Maximilian Beiser, Yiyang Zhi, Nikola Opa c ˇ \mathrm{\check{c}} ak, Marco Piccardo, Benedikt Schwarz, Federico Capasso
arxiv-2206-03379.description: Abstract Rapid development of Fabry-Perot quantum cascade laser frequency combs has converted them from laboratory devices to key components of next-generation fast molecular spectrometers. Recently, free-running ring quantum cascade lasers allowed generation of new frequency comb states induced by phase turbulence.

arxiv-2211-08037.title: Mirror-reflective algebras and Tachikawa’s second conjecture
arxiv-2211-08037.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by . Given an algebra with an idempotent, we introduce two procedures to construct families of new algebras, termed mirror-reflective algebras and reduced mirror-reflective algebras. We then establish connections among these algebras by recollements of derived module categories. In case of given algebras being gendo-symmetric, we show that the (reduced) mirror-reflective algebras are symmetric and provide new methods to construct systematically both higher dimensional (minimal) Auslander-Gorenstein algebras and gendo-symmetric algebras of higher dominant dimensions.

arxiv-2304-13984.title: An FPTAS for Budgeted Laminar Matroid Independent Set
arxiv-2304-13984.creator: Ilan Doron-Arad, Ariel Kulik, Hadas Shachnai
arxiv-2304-13984.description: Abstract We study the budgeted laminar matroid independent set problem. The input is a ground set, where each element has a cost and a non-negative profit, along with a laminar matroid over the elements and a budget. The goal is to select a maximum profit independent set of the matroid whose total cost is bounded by the budget.

arxiv-2308-01604.title: IndoHerb: Indonesia Medicinal Plants Recognition using Transfer Learning and Deep Learning
arxiv-2308-01604.creator: Muhammad Salman Ikrar Musyaffa’, Novanto Yudistira, Muhammad Arif Rahman, Jati Batoro
arxiv-2308-01604.description: Abstract The rich diversity of herbal plants in Indonesia holds immense potential as alternative resources for traditional healing and ethnobotanical practices. However, the dwindling recognition of herbal plants due to modernization poses a significant challenge in preserving this valuable heritage.

arxiv-2408-07955.title: GERestaurant: A German Dataset of Annotated Restaurant Reviews for Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis
arxiv-2408-07955.creator: Nils Constantin Hellwig, Jakob Fehle, Markus Bink, Christian Wolff
arxiv-2408-07955.description: Abstract We present GERestaurant, a novel dataset consisting of 3,078 German language restaurant reviews manually annotated for Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA). All reviews were collected from Tripadvisor, covering a diverse selection of restaurants, including regional and international cuisine with various culinary styles.

arxiv-2503-15240.title: Powerfully embedded subgroups of extensions of powerful pro- p p groups and its applications to automorphisms of finite groups
arxiv-2503-15240.creator: Sathasivam Kalithasan, Tony N. Mavely, Viji Z. Thomas
arxiv-2503-15240.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Sathasivam Kalithasan, Tony N. Mavely, Viji Z. Thomas. One of the aims of this paper is to obtain structural results showing that powerful subgroups are abundant in pro- p p groups admitting certain powerful quotients.

arxiv-2504-05718.title: CVA6-VMRT: A Modular Approach Towards Time-Predictable Virtual Memory in a 64-bit Application Class RISC-V Processor
arxiv-2504-05718.creator: Christopher Reinwardt, Robert Balas, Alessandro Ottaviano, Angelo Garofalo, Luca Benini
arxiv-2504-05718.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Christopher Reinwardt, Robert Balas, Alessandro Ottaviano, Angelo Garofalo, Luca Benini. The increasing complexity of autonomous systems has driven a shift to integrated heterogeneous SoCs with real-time and safety demands. Ensuring deterministic WCETs and low-latency for critical tasks requires minimizing interference on shared resources like virtual memory. Existing techniques, such as software coloring and memory replication, introduce significant area and performance overhead, especially with virtualized memory where address translation adds latency uncertainty.

arxiv-2505-03609.title: Global well-posedness in the critical Besov space of the skew mean curvature flow in ℝ d : d ≥ 5 \mathbb{R}^{d}:d\geq 5
arxiv-2505-03609.creator: Ning-An Lai, Jie Shao, Zexian Zhang, Yi Zhou
arxiv-2505-03609.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ning-An Lai, Jie Shao, Zexian Zhang, Yi Zhou. In this paper we prove small-data global well-posedness for the skew mean curvature flow of codimension-two submanifolds of ℝ d + 2 \mathbb{R}^{d+2} ( d ≥ 5 d\geq 5 ) in the critical Besov space. With harmonic coordinates and Coulomb gauge, the flow is formulated as a quasilinear Schrödinger equation for the complex mean curvature coupled to an elliptic system for the geometric and gauge variables.

arxiv-2506-13827.title: Balancing Preservation and Modification: A Region and Semantic-Aware Metric for Instruction-Based Image Editing
arxiv-2506-13827.creator: Zhuoying Li, Zhu Xu, Yuxin Peng, Yang Liu
arxiv-2506-13827.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Zhuoying Li, Zhu Xu, Yuxin Peng, Yang Liu. Instruction-based image editing, which aims to modify the image faithfully towards instruction while preserving irrelevant content unchanged, has made advanced progresses. However, there still lacks a comprehensive metric for assessing the editing quality. Existing metrics either require high costs concerning human evaluation, which hinders large-scale evaluation, or adapt from other tasks and lose specified concerns, failing to comprehensively evaluate the modification of instruction and the preservation of irrelevant regions, resulting in biased evaluation.

arxiv-2511-11524.title: The Interoperability Challenge in DFT Workflows Across Implementations
arxiv-2511-11524.creator: Simon K. Steensen, Tushar Singh Thakur, Manuel Dillenz, Johan M. Carlsson, Celso R. C. Rêgo, Eibar Flores, Hamid Hajiyani, Felix Hanke, Juan María García Lastra, Wolfgang Wenzel, Nicola Marzari, Tejs Vegge, Giovanni Pizzi, Ivano E. Castelli
arxiv-2511-11524.description: Abstract Interoperability and cross-validation remains a significant challenge in the computational materials discovery community. In this context, we introduce a common input/output standard designed for internal translation by various workflow managers (AiiDA, PerQueue, Pipeline Pilot, and SimStack) to produce results in a unified schema.

pmc-11715109.title: Evaluating Life Simple Seven’s Influence on Brain Health Outcomes: The Intersection of Lifestyle and Dementia
pmc-11715109.creator: Diandra N. Denier‐Fields, Ronald E. Gagnon, Brenda Ryther, Ian A. Canovi, Diane Wilkinson, Lia J. Sparks, Leonardo A. Rivera‐Rivera, Tobey J. Betthauser, Barbara B. Bendlin, Sterling C. Johnson, Corinne D. Engelman
pmc-11715109.description: BackgroundLifestyle factors have been studied for their role in dementia, but few have comprehensively assessed both Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and cerebrovascular disease (CBVD) pathologies. This study innovatively integrates AD, CBVD, and cognitive composite scores (CCS) within the same cohort to investigate the association of the Life Simple Seven (LS7) score with a broad spectrum of dementia‐related outcomes.

pmc-12290810.title: Cerebellar non-invasive stimulation of social and emotional mentalizing: A meta-analysis
pmc-12290810.creator: Frank Van Overwalle, Naem Haihambo, Qianying Ma, Meijia Li, Rocío Martínez-Regueiro, Ines Argoub, Mahyar Firouzi, Natacha Deroost, Chris Baeken, Kris Baetens
pmc-12290810.description: The present meta-analysis investigated the impact of non-invasive stimulation, using transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) and transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) targeting the posterior cerebellum, on social and emotional mentalizing about others. Prior research has convincingly shown that the posterior cerebellum supports social and emotional cognition. We identified 14 studies targeting the cerebellum with appropriate control conditions (i.e.

pmc-12409887.title: Navigating ethical challenges in digital transformation: insights on climate adaptation, microbiology, healthcare, robotics, and AI under the EU AI act: an experts panel discussion
pmc-12409887.creator: Saeed M. Alghamdi, Okpala Charles Chikwendu, Okafor Ugochukwu Chukwuma, Daniel Otieno Okech, Modestus O. Okwu, Samina Khalid, Aggeliki Vlachostergiou
pmc-12409887.description: The ethical complexities of technological advancement are growing as fields such as climate adaptation, microbiology, healthcare, robotics, and artificial intelligence (AI) evolve rapidly. While these technologies offer innovative solutions to global challenges, they raise significant ethical concerns. In climate adaptation, AI-driven models and remote sensing technologies prompt questions about data privacy, environmental justice, and equitable access, especially for vulnerable populations.

pmc-12514626.title: US Coverage Changes During Medicaid Unwinding in 2023
pmc-12514626.creator: Adrianna McIntyre, Molly Morein, Jinwoo Kim, Jose F. Figueroa, Benjamin D. Sommers
pmc-12514626.description: Key PointsQuestionHow did coverage losses during unwinding of the Medicaid continuous coverage provision vary across different measures, states, and demographic groups?FindingsIn this cross-sectional study, net Medicaid enrollment loss during unwinding varied substantially across states and was lower than the sum of terminations during this time.

pmc-12822093.title: Weighting strategy and selection analysis in the panel ‘Health in Germany‘: methods and results for the 2024 annual survey
pmc-12822093.creator: Stefan Damerow, Ronny Kuhnert, Angelika Schaffrath Rosario, Johannes Lemcke
pmc-12822093.description: BackgroundThe panel `Health in Germany` has been established to gather nationwide health-related information, replacing cross-sectional surveys as primary data sources. However, panel designs involve multiple selection stages, potentially introducing additional nonresponse bias. This study aims to describe this drop-out bias and the weighting strategy used to improve representativeness.MethodsPanelists were recruited through a recruitment study.

pmc-13226696.title: A multi-task information extraction Chinese dataset for APT cyber threat intelligence
pmc-13226696.creator: Lu Sun, Ga Xiang, Zicheng Tan, Zhaozhong Guo, Rui Qi, Jun Cao
pmc-13226696.description: Advanced Persistent Threats(APTs) are characterized by persistence and complex attack chains. Information extraction techniques enable the identification of critical knowledge from unstructured Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI), improving the detection of APT attacks. At present, high-quality information extraction Chinese datasets for APT scenarios remain scarce, particularly those covering multiple tasks such as entity, relation, and event extraction.

pmc-13264795.title: Fertility outcomes and management of long-term pubertal testosterone replacement sequelae in Oliver-McFarlane syndrome: a case report and literature review
pmc-13264795.creator: Shlomi Moshe, Yoram Dekel, Galia Oron, Maharan Kabha
pmc-13264795.description: BackgroundOliver-McFarlane syndrome (OMCS) is an extremely rare autosomal recessive disorder caused by biallelic mutations in the PNPLA6 gene, characterized by retinal dystrophy, trichomegaly, neurodevelopmental impairment, and combined pituitary hormone deficiencies. Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (HH) is a frequent endocrine manifestation; however, the long-term reproductive consequences and fertility potential in affected males have not been previously described.

pmc-13351392.title: A notes bivariate power law processes: conditional intensity and parameter estimation techniques,☆☆☆

The point process model effectively represents the number of random events occurring over time through its intensity function. When events are of two types, a bivariate point process allows simultaneous analysis of each event’s intensity.

pmc-13461295.creator: Farsana Mustafa, Jacky Ganguly, Ayush Agarwal, Sayoni Roy Chowdhury, Surojit Ruidas, Ajay Garg, Debayan Dutta, Divya M Radhakrishnan, Hrishikesh Kumar, Achal Kumar Srivastava, Divyani Garg

pmc-13585405.title: Cirrhosis Impairs Reconstitution of the Circulating T‐Lymphocyte Compartment After Direct‐Acting Antiviral Therapy for Hepatitis C Virus Infection
pmc-13585405.creator: Lorena Paule, Elisa Castillo, Leticia Muñoz, Javier Martínez, Carlos Fernández, Alejandro Miranda, Margaret Lario, Jorge Monserrat, Miguel Ángel Ortega, José Luis Calleja, Melchor Álvarez‐Mon, Agustín Albillos
pmc-13585405.description: BackgroundDirect‐acting antivirals (DAAs) achieve sustained virological response (SVR) in over 95% of patients with chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection. Although viral eradication allows partial immune restoration, it remains unclear whether established cirrhosis limits recovery of the circulating T lymphocyte compartment after SVR.

pmc-13628979.title: A review of Hallermann-Streiff syndrome demonstrates clinical overlap with other conditions
pmc-13628979.creator: Caroline Cavender, Carrie Atzinger, Anne Slavotinek
pmc-13628979.description: Hallermann-Streiff syndrome (HSS) is a rare genetic condition characterized by seven cardinal findings comprising congenital cataracts, microphthalmia, recognizable facial features, sparse hair with hypotrichosis, skin atrophy, dental anomalies, and short stature. Around 200 patients have been reported and almost all cases have been sporadic.
